bib.title: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 11048-11064

question: Which aspects of the demonstrations in in-context learning actually drive end-task performance, and does the ground-truth input-label mapping matter?
hypothesis: Ground-truth input-label pairings are not what drives in-context learning gains; the label space, the input text distribution and the pair format are (stated as findings, not framed as an a-priori hypothesis).
contributions: Show that replacing gold labels with random labels barely hurts in-context learning across 12 models including GPT-3
Identify label space, input distribution and format as the key drivers via ablated demonstration variants
Show meta-training with an in-context objective magnifies reliance on simpler aspects such as format

method.summary: Inference-only study. Demonstrations are altered (random labels, a% correct labels, OOD inputs, random English words as labels, no labels, labels only) and performance is compared with gold-label demos and no demos across 12 model/inference-method variants on 26 datasets.
method.task: in-context learning on classification and multi-choice tasks

datasets.name: 26 low-resource datasets (GLUE, SuperGLUE, financial_phrasebank, poem_sentiment, ethos, tweet_eval, openbookqa, commonsense_qa, ai2_arc, copa, etc.)
datasets.size: each with fewer than 10K training examples; Table 2 gives per-dataset # train / # eval (e.g. financial_phrasebank 1,811/453, hate_speech18 8,562/2,141)
datasets.split: k=16 examples sampled uniformly from train; HuggingFace development data used for evaluation
datasets.source: HuggingFace datasets (Lhoest et al., 2021); same k-shot train sets and 5 seeds as Min et al. 2021b
datasets.preprocessing: minimal templates (Table 3); manual templates as ablation

datasets.name: CC-News
datasets.size: external corpus for OOD demonstration inputs, sampled to match test input length

datasets.name: english-words (pypi)
datasets.size: 61,569 words, source of random English labels

other.note: eval datasets do not overlap meta-training datasets
size assumed 175B following Gao et al. 2021 and Artetxe et al. 2021; weights not public

inference.decoding: argmax over a small discrete label set C of P(y|x1,y1...xk,yk,x) (direct); channel flips x and y
inference.samples: 5 random seeds for the choice of k training examples (3 seeds and 6 datasets for fairseq 13B and GPT-3); per-dataset average over seeds, then macro-average over datasets
inference.prompting: k=16 input-label demonstrations, minimal templates; GPT-2 separates input and label with a space and examples with a space; MetaICL, GPT-J, GPT-3 use newline between input and label and three newlines between examples; fairseq uses a newline for both

parameters.ablation_datasets: 5 classification (MRPC, RTE, Tweet_eval-hate, SICK, poem-sentiment) and 4 multi-choice (OpenbookQA, CommonsenseQA, COPA, ARC)
parameters.random_label_sampling: uniform from C; Appendix C.2 also samples from true label distribution

other.hardware_note: fairseq 13B and GPT-3 restricted to 6 datasets and 3 seeds due to limited resources

metrics.name: Macro-F1
metrics.definition: classification tasks; averaged over seeds per dataset then macro-averaged over datasets

eval.protocol: Variants differ in format/input/label-space/mapping (Fig 7, Fig 8-10 tables); no significance test described beyond use of the word significantly

prompts.text: sentence 1: Cisco pared spending to compensate for sluggish sales . [SEP] sentence 2: In response to sluggish sales , Cisco pared spending . \n {equivalent|not_equivalent}
Cisco pared spending to compensate for sluggish sales . \n The question is: In response to sluggish sales , Cisco pared spending . True or False? \n The answer is:{True|False}

results.claim: Replacing gold labels with random labels in demonstrations drops performance only 0-5% absolute across nearly all models.
results.setup: Channel/direct inference; k=16 minimal-template demonstrations; 12 model variants (6 LMs x direct/channel), 26 classification and multi-choice datasets (6 datasets for fairseq 13B and GPT-3); Macro-F1 for classification, accuracy for multi-choice
results.quote: models see performance drop in the range of 0–5% absolute

results.claim: Average drop from random labels is smaller in multi-choice than classification.
results.setup: Channel/direct inference; k=16 minimal-template demonstrations; 12 model variants (6 LMs x direct/channel), 26 classification and multi-choice datasets (6 datasets for fairseq 13B and GPT-3); Macro-F1 for classification, accuracy for multi-choice
results.quote: There is less impact in replacing labels in multi-choice tasks (1.7% on average) than in classification tasks (2.6% absolute).

results.claim: MetaICL shows almost no drop from random labels.
results.setup: Channel/direct inference; k=16 minimal-template demonstrations; 12 model variants (6 LMs x direct/channel), 26 classification and multi-choice datasets (6 datasets for fairseq 13B and GPT-3); Macro-F1 for classification, accuracy for multi-choice; MetaICL only

results.claim: Always-incorrect labels preserve most of the demonstration gain for MetaICL (classification), MetaICL (multi-choice) and GPT-J (multi-choice).
results.setup: Ablation, 5 classification and 4 multi-choice datasets, k=16, 0% correct labels

results.claim: GPT-J on classification drops nearly 10% with always-incorrect labels but stays above no demonstrations.
Gold-vs-random gap stays small across k; gains from larger k flatten beyond k=8.
results.unit: % gap across k (4.4% at k=4 classification)
results.setup: Channel MetaICL (classification) and Direct GPT-J (multi-choice), k in 0,4,8,16,32

results.claim: OOD inputs (CC-News sentences) in demonstrations cut performance by 3-16% absolute, showing the input distribution matters.
results.setup: Channel MetaICL, Direct GPT-J, Channel GPT-J; classification and multi-choice; Direct MetaICL is an exception

results.claim: For direct models, random English words as labels instead of random in-label-space labels cost 5-16% absolute, showing the label space matters.
results.setup: Direct models, classification and multi-choice, ablation datasets

results.claim: For channel models removing the label space costs little.
Direct MetaICL keeps 95% (classification) and 82% (multi-choice) of the in-context gain using random corpus sentences randomly paired with the label set.
results.setup: Direct MetaICL; OOD inputs + random labels vs gold demos
results.quote: it is possible to retain 95% and 82% of improve

results.claim: Channel models keep 75-87% of the gain by pairing each unlabeled training input with a random English word.
results.setup: MetaICL cls, GPT-J cls, MetaICL multi-choice, GPT-J multi-choice (channel)
results.quote: retain 82%, 87%, 86% and 75% of improvements from in-context

results.claim: Removing the format (no labels, or labels only) is close to or worse than no demonstrations.
results.setup: Direct/channel MetaICL and GPT-J, ablation datasets
results.quote: removing the format is close to or worse than no demonstrations

results.claim: Sampling random labels from the true label distribution narrows the gold-vs-random gap further for Channel MetaICL.
results.setup: Classification, Channel MetaICL, uniform vs true-distribution random labels
results.quote: with Channel MetaICL, the gap is reduced from 1.9% to 1.3% absolute
the gap is reduced from 5.0% to 3.5% absolute

results.claim: Largest per-dataset gold-vs-random gap is nearly 14% absolute on financial_phrasebank with GPT-J.

limits: Only classification and multi-choice tasks with natural-language inputs; generation not tested (authors concede)
Synthetic tasks may use ground-truth labels more (Rong 2021)
Macro averages hide outlier datasets such as financial_phrasebank (nearly 14% gap) and some hate-speech sets
Later work: Kim et al. 2022 found negated labels substantially lower classification performance; Madaan and Yazdanbakhsh 2022 found random rationales in chain-of-thought hurt substantially
Models of 774M-175B from 2021-era; no instruction-tuned models (authors only hypothesise findings carry over)
Several direct models (GPT-2, GPT-J, fairseq 6.7B) are near random guessing on many classification datasets; channel fairseq 13B no-demo beats gold demos
GPT-3 and fairseq 13B evaluated on only 6 datasets and 3 seeds
Temperature, max tokens and seeds values not stated; GPT-3 size assumed 175B

terms.definition: correctly-paired inputs and labels in the demonstrations
direct models P(y|x); channel models condition on the label and score the input (x and y flipped)
training with an in-context learning objective on a collection of supervised datasets (MetaICL)
